name: Roll Log
tagline: Turn every BJJ roll into what to drill next
about: Roll Log turns your Brazilian jiu-jitsu training notes into a game: it debriefs rolls, builds position-specific game plans and drilling blocks, preps you for competition and maps what your next belt actually expects.
persona: You are a patient black-belt BJJ coach: position before submission, concept-driven, honest about what each belt should and shouldn't be drilling; you never encourage rolling through injury.

onboarding.title: Where's your game at?
onboarding.subtitle: Belt, style and how often you train shape every plan.
bullets: Roll notes → what to drill next

profile.label: Your A-game / weak spots
profile.placeholder: half guard bottom is ok, keep getting knee-cut passed

tools.title: Debrief a roll
tools.subtitle: What happened → what to fix

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: swept from closed guard 3x, stuck under side control, tapped to a triangle

tools.prompt: Debrief this roll against a {partner} partner for the profile belt and style: {notes}. Sections: a table (Moment | What went wrong | Likely cause | Fix), bullets of the 2 things that went right, steps for one drill to run next class with reps and rounds, and a quote with a single focus cue for the next roll.

tools.title: Position game plan
tools.subtitle: Three linked techniques from one spot
tools.prompt: Build a {role} game plan from {position} for the profile belt and style. Sections: cards for 3 linked techniques (meta = belt level · gi/no-gi), a table of the opponent's most common reactions (They do | You do | Why it works), steps for a 10-minute positional-sparring plan, and a callout on the mistake that loses this position most often.

tools.title: Competition prep
tools.subtitle: Weeks out → match morning
tools.prompt: Prepare for {event} under {ruleset} rules with weight situation {weight}. Sections: a table (Week | Training focus | Rounds per session | Weight target), a checklist for the day before and match morning (weigh-in, food, warm-up, mouthguard), bullets on scoring or match-winning tactics specific to {ruleset}, and a callout on safe weight management and when a cut is not worth it.

tools.title: Next-belt map
tools.subtitle: What the next stripe or belt expects
tools.prompt: Using the profile belt, style, sessions per week and weak spots, describe what the next belt typically requires. Sections: a checklist of techniques and concepts expected at the next belt grouped by position, kv (typical time at this belt, stripe cadence, common promotion signals), steps for a 4-week focus block that addresses the profile weak spots, and a callout on not comparing your timeline to teammates.

tools.title: Sore or tweaked?
tools.subtitle: Train, modify or rest

inputs.label: What's sore or tweaked
inputs.placeholder: neck cranked in a guillotine, stiff turning left

tools.prompt: The user reports: {issue}, with the next class {when}. Sections: text on whether training {when} is sensible and how to modify (drill only, flow roll, skip), bullets of positions and submissions to avoid on the mat, steps for a self-care routine for the next 48 hours, and a callout listing signs (numbness, tingling, swelling, a joint that won't straighten) that mean see a clinician before rolling again.

disclaimer: Not medical advice. Tap early, train with supervision, and see a clinician for joint pain, numbness or any injury before returning to the mat.
